Finite input contract. Assume the pinned manuscript supplies: (S1) arbitrarily
small smooth finite-cutoff path avoidance in the conformal fixed-area gauge;
(S2) exact-double-preserving finite-cutoff repairs and a nonzero split/coupling
first variation; (S3) every sufficiently high adjacent pair, including consecutive
round-degree blocks, admits the designated isolated double in arbitrarily prescribed
fixed smooth neighborhoods of round. These are its Lemmas 2.1-2.5 and the fixed-area
gauge preceding them. Their correctness was not independently established here.
The exact polar Ricci identities, elliptic whole-ball Dirichlet theory and spectral
functional calculus are also used, with their proofs or derivations described below
and in the independent supplement. No all-spectrum or growing-degree uniform input
is assumed.

The strict >c can be weakened to >=c without changing the construction.

POST-SOURCE COMMON-METRIC STATUS — 2026-10-08

This is the current status after reading all three final spectral reports and
LATE_GEOMETRY_HIGH_LEVEL_AUDIT_v1.txt. FINAL_STATUS.txt is preserved as the
earlier historical freeze, when those reports were still pending. PROOF_v2.txt
is also preserved; PROOF_v3.txt contains the repaired argument and the exact
pre-Moser control-coordinate clarification.

CURRENT CLAIM CLASS
Internally reconstructed candidate common-metric theorem, supported by separate
internal source, transfer, uniformity and high-level integration audits. The
finite spectral input gates S1-S3 are now internally discharged jointly by the
three source reports below. No remaining source/transfer obstruction was found
within their precise interfaces. This is not formal proof or external expert
validation; external validity and historical novelty/priority remain UNKNOWN.
No established major-result or global open-problem-resolution claim is made.

EXACT CANDIDATE THEOREM
For every 4/9<v<1 and 1<c<9v/4 there is one complete smooth metric g on R^3,
Euclidean near the origin, with Ric>=0 and AVR(g)=v, such that
  limsup_{k integer -> infinity} h_k(R^3,g)/(k+1)^2 > c.
The same g serves an unbounded degree sequence; it may depend on v and c.
There is no endpoint or full-limit conclusion. Its repeated nonisometric links
give nonunique tangent cones, so Huang's unique-cone coefficient does not apply.

SOURCE INPUT CLOSURE AND REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
S1: spectral_transversality_audit/REPORT.txt reconstructs fixed-area restoration,
pair trace-free rank two, and finite-cutoff smooth relative path density. Fixed
simple collars must already be simple. Even paths avoid multiplicities only
within the two separate parity lists; cross-parity equalities remain permitted.
S2: spectral_exact_double_audit/REPORT.txt reconstructs finite repair retaining
an isolated exact double, a C^2 Banach slice restricted to smooths, and the
countable all-other-simple crossing construction. Its curve space fixes the
double value and first jet, not an entire crossing neighborhood. Endpoints are
free or already all-spectrum simple. The control direction is u_1*u_2 in
PRE-GAUGE conformal coordinates; its nonzero compression is transported by Moser.
S3: spectral_crossblock_audit/REPORT.txt, including final Section 11, reconstructs
Lemma 2.4, the cross-block inversion and parity index plac
